note_claims.claim: Head injury after a mechanical fall at home at about 09:30.
Patient tripped on a rug and struck the left side of her head on a door frame.
Daughter reports the patient seemed muddled for about 10 minutes afterwards.
Patient has no memory of the muddled period.
Loss of consciousness is uncertain (unwitnessed).
Patient had one episode of vomiting in the car.
Patient experienced a mild headache at the impact site.
Patient had no visual disturbance, limb weakness, or neck pain.
Patient had no preceding dizziness or presyncope.
Last apixaban dose was taken this morning, after the fall.
Patient had tetanus up to date.
Patient is prescribed Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
Patient is prescribed Amiloride 5 mg once daily.
Patient is allergic to penicillin (swelling).
Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) is 15.
There is a 3 cm laceration with a haematoma over the right temple.
Pupils are equal and reactive to light.
Strength is normal everywhere (normal power in all limbs).
No cervical spine midline tenderness.
Heart rate is irregular at about 80.
Blood pressure is 146/82.
Head injury in an anticoagulated 81-year-old with brief post-traumatic confusion and amnesia, and one episode of vomiting.
CT head scan is required (anticoagulated).
This evening's dose of apixaban will be withheld until the CT head scan is reviewed.
The wound will be cleaned and closed with steri-strips.
Discharge with the daughter is contingent on a normal CT scan.
Call 999 or return immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Written head injury advice was given to the daughter.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician introduced herself as Dr Pemberton.
The relative is the patient's daughter, Sue.
The patient tripped on the rug in the hall and banged her head on the door frame.
The patient initially stated the time of the fall was about half past nine.
The relative corrected the time, stating it was about quarter to eight, noting the post hadn't come and the patient hadn't had breakfast.
The patient acknowledged the relative's correction.
The patient stated the injury was on the left side, by their eye.
The patient stated they did not think they had blacked out.
The relative reported that the patient was muddled for about ten minutes after the fall, kept asking what day it was.
The patient stated they did not remember the daughter arriving.
The relative reported that the patient was sick once in the car on the way to the clinic.
The patient denied being sick in the car.
The patient reported a bit of a headache where they hit it.
The patient denied problems with vision, weakness in arms or legs.
The patient denied neck pain.
The patient stated they caught their foot on the rug and were not dizzy.
The relative stated the patient is on Apixaban 2.5 milligrams twice a day for heart rhythm, Bisoprolol 2.5 milligrams once a day, and Amlodipine 5 mg.
The patient stated they last took the Apixaban this morning with their breakfast, after the fall.
The patient stated they are allergic to penicillin, which causes swelling.
Examination findings include a Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) of 15.
Examination findings include a 3 cm laceration with a bump around it on the left temple.
Examination findings include equal and reactive pupils.
Examination findings include normal power in all limbs.
Examination findings include no cervical spine midline tenderness.
The patient's heart rate is irregular at about 80.
The patient's blood pressure is 146 over 82.
The clinician advised a CT scan of the head because the patient is on a blood thinner and needs to rule out internal bleeding.
The clinician decided to hold off the evening's dose of Apixaban until the CT scan is reviewed.
The plan is to clean the cut and close it with steri-strips.
If the CT scan is normal, the patient can go home with the daughter, who will stay with her for 24 hours.
Safety netting advice includes calling 999 or returning immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
